transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marcus Varela (CTO, Alcyon), Lena Ortiz (ML Platform Lead), Samir Patel (SRE), Rui Chen (Product)

---
Summary (auto): Walkthrough of model catalog features oriented at edge/near-edge deployments. Focus on interpreting bench signals, using the compatibility matrix to map quantized kernels to Alcyon GPUs, and discussing tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Topics covered: model selection for edge GPUs; bench spreadsheet explanation; quantization and kernel compatibility; routing/fallbacks for limited memory; private deployment checklist; pricing contours for Dedicated.

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
00:00 Jordan: okay everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. we've got Priya from SE who will walk through the catalog and the bench stuff. Marcus, Lena, Samir, Rui, thanks for making time.
00:34 Marcus: yep thanks, appreciate it. we pushed this to the calendar because Alcyon is evaluating run-time options for inference at the edge, our main drivers are p99 under 300ms and keeping token cost under a very tight envelope for inference per user session.
01:05 Priya: great, that's helpful — i'll circle back to those success criteria when we look at the bench numbers. quick agenda: catalog demo, pick candidate open models, show bench results and comp matrix, then discuss deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and next steps. sound good?
01:35 Lena: yeah that works. one thing — we have Ampere A10Gs in our pods and a couple of Jetson-like devices for ultra-edge, so kernel/quantization compatibility is huge for us. also data residency: some telemetry can't leave the eu region.
02:10 Priya: perfect, we'll call out those constraints. quick note — some of the names in the UI are auto-normalized so you might see slight differences; the runtime supports kernel variants for tflite-ish and custom quant kernels, we call them in the matrix as q8, q4f etc which sometimes shows up as q4fl or q4f-legacy in the export, little inconsistencies in the transcription here, ignore naming drift.
02:52 Jordan: also flagged that for enterprise customers we can do a Private control plane in a VPC plus on-prem package if needed, with KMS integration.
03:12 Samir: ok good. about the bench spreadsheet — when you say 'bench' is that synthetic tokens or replaying our traces? because synthetic sometimes hides patterns.
03:37 Priya: great question. the spreadsheet has two tabs: microbench synthetic (latency/throughput on canonical prompts) and trace-replay (if you provide traces we'll run a realistic replay and surface p50/p95/p99 and token cost). ideally we get both.
04:05 Rui: we can provide traces, but note we strip PII and obfuscate. timeline — we want a pilot in the next 6 weeks if benches look good.
04:28 Priya: cool. i'll note action for Marcus to share traces.
04:42 Jordan: alright i'm going to share my screen — show the catalog UI. (screen sharing) this is the model catalog — filters on the left, performance profiles in the center, and a compatibility heatmap to the right.
05:12 Priya: the filters you want to use for edge are: max params, tokenization type, and hardware compatibility. we also have an 'Optimize suggested profiles' button that proposes quantization and kernel variants based on your pong length distribution.
05:42 Lena: show me how you pick a candidate.
05:51 Priya: sure — for Alcyon i'd pick a small open model family first — for example 'Orchid-7B' variants. click the model, then the 'benchmarks' tab.
06:20 Priya: here you can see microbench numbers — note these were run on our standard A100 cluster, so the absolute latencies differ on your A10G. the important columns are model variant, quantization profile, memory footprint, and tokens/sec. we also show cost-per-1k-tokens assuming our hosted runtime price or you can switch to Dedicated math to see commit pricing.
07:02 Marcus: i'm seeing q4f numbers that look promising but i'm worried about q4f compatibility on our Nvidia A10G, does the heatmap show kernel support?
07:30 Priya: yes — heatmap maps compiled kernel variants to hardware targets. for the A10G it shows q4f via cuBLAS-optimized kernels but with a note: requires patched libcudnn on older drivers; that's why the matrix attaches a 'compat note' column. sometimes our export shows driver names slightly differently (e.g., cuDNN -> cudn) — testing note.
08:05 Samir: we run an older cluster for cost reasons, 470 driver series, will that be an issue?
08:22 Priya: probably for some q4 variants. for those we recommend q8 or q4f-legacy—there's a small latency penalty but better compatibility. you'll see fallback routing in the Runtime where requests auto-route to a compatible variant if the preferred kernel not available.
08:55 Jordan: the routing fallbacks are important — if the primary variant isn't available we route to a compatible variant or to a hosted low-cost fallback so your app stays up.
09:18 Lena: can we pin a model version? our release cadence requires predictable output for compliance.
09:30 Priya: yes you can pin model version + quant profile in the deployment config and create rollout policies (canary/A-B). the Console stores per-route metrics and you can tie evals to prompt sets to detect regressions.
09:52 Rui: what about embeddings? we use them for semantic search and want to ensure embedding dimensionality doesn't change across quantization.
10:08 Priya: embeddings are produced deterministically from the model head. quantization shouldn't change dimension but might affect numeric precision — we recommend a small eval set to measure downstream recall. Optimize has a 'embedding drift' monitor you can enable.
10:40 Marcus: show me an example of bench interpretation — the sheet we got earlier had two rows with similar token/sec but different p99s.
11:00 Priya: right, token/sec is throughput but p99 captures tail latency. look at columns: mean_kv_cache_miss_rate and batch_fill_factor — if you have a distribution with many short requests, batching is low and p99 suffers. the Optimize suggestions include prefix caching and per-route batching thresholds.
11:40 Jordan: also note KV cache hit rates — for chat style apps caching drastically drops token cost; the console shows token-level cost breakdown per route.
12:05 Marcus: how do we reason about the cost of on-device quantized models vs Hosted? per-token cost on hosted looks higher but infra ops are zero for us.
12:29 Priya: hosting has higher per-token price but no infra maintenance; Dedicated gives you lower unit cost at commit; Private adds compliance but upfront OPEX. we ran a hypothetical: at your peak 200 qps, Dedicated with our suggested batching had ~35% lower token cost than hosted. we'll send that sheet.
12:58 Samir: in Dedicated, can we still have fallback to Redwood hosted if we hit capacity spikes?
13:10 Jordan: yes, there's an automated overflow policy — you can set burst to hosted with data-exfiltration controls. for sensitive requests you can set a policy to always fail rather than route to hosted.
13:40 Lena: what about observability — we want request tracing per token for audits.
13:55 Priya: Console has per-request traces, token cost, and you can export to your SIEM. audit logs and SSO (SAML) supported; SOC2 report available on request.
14:25 Rui: ok back to catalog — show compatibility matrix export.
14:40 Priya: exporting yields a csv with columns: model, variant, quant_profile, kernel_variant, hw_target, notes. note: the csv sometimes mangles kernel_variant names (we're tracking a fix). here's an export link (sample): https://redwood.ai/bench/ALCY-edge-v1.xlsx
15:12 Marcus: thanks. can you walk through the 'Optimize suggested profiles' output for Orchid-7B?
15:28 Priya: sure — it suggests q4f with per-route batch size 1-4 for low latency, kv prefix caching enabled for chat flows, and a fall-back to q8 for older drivers. it also recommends a small retrain for the tokenizer to reduce unknown tokens for your domain, which cuts token count ~3-5% in our tests.
16:05 Samir: token reduction would save cost if it's 5%, yes. for p99 targets we need end-to-end including network hop to the device.
16:30 Jordan: network matters a lot; for geo edge devices colocating a lightweight runtime reduces network hops. we have a Private on-prem package that deploys inference runtime in your cluster behind your VPC.
16:58 Lena: that pack includes KMS? we need rotation and HSM for keys.
17:10 Priya: yes KMS integration is supported, HSM connectors possible in Private. we can provide compliance docs. Jordan will share SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
17:35 Rui: what's the usual pilot size? we need a realistic staging plan.
17:45 Jordan: customers do a 4-week pilot: week1 trace collection and small synthetic benches, week2 trace replay and variant selection, week3 Dedicated/private proof-of-concept configuration, week4 stability and SLA smoke tests. we'll tailor it to you.
18:10 Marcus: that fits our internal timeline. one question — does Redwood Optimize recommend quant profiles dynamically or is it a human-reviewed suggestion?
18:28 Priya: Optimize suggests profiles based on offline analysis of your traces and model behavior — it's automated but our SEs review for safety and semantic quality tradeoffs. you can opt into auto-deploy or require manual approval.
19:00 Samir: show me the runtime fallback policy UI — do we get logs when fallback happens?
19:15 Priya: yes, there's an event stream and route-level metrics with tags for fallback reason (kernel missing, capacity, etc.). we can stream to your cloudwatch or splunk.
19:45 Marcus: are there any limitations around open models licenses we should consider? some of our legal folks asked about permissible uses.
20:05 Jordan: we provide license metadata in the catalog; for each model we list license type and any caveats. for enterprise we can help analyze.
20:28 Rui: demo the A/B rollout for a quant profile change.
20:40 Priya: (click) here's the rollout config — you can select percentage, define evaluation metrics (e.g., p99, semantic-quality threshold) and set auto-rollback criteria. note: evals run against your registered prompt set.
21:18 Lena: what about quantization-induced hallucinations? we've seen some regressions with aggressive quant.
21:35 Priya: good point — aggressive quant can change logits slightly. Optimize includes a regression test harness that shows delta in rouge/bleu/embedding-similarity and flags regressions. we also recommend human eval on a small safety prompt set.
22:05 Marcus: how do we instrument cost across multiple regions? we have EU and NA regions with different infra pricing.
22:25 Jordan: Console supports per-region cost breakdown, and you can create routing policies by region, TL;DR: you can force EU requests to EU private cluster.
22:50 Samir: can you do on-device Jetson inference via cross-compile?
23:05 Priya: we support cross-compiled runtimes for certain ultra-edge devices; for tiny devices we recommend offloading to nearby gateway nodes. the catalog flags models with Jetson-compatible kernels. sometimes names show as 'jetson-nano-x' in exports, please ignore small naming diffs.
23:40 Rui: ok let's pick two candidates for the pilot — one high-accuracy 7B q4f and one smaller 3B q8 that should be safe on older drivers.
23:58 Priya: perfect plan — we'll run benches for both and produce a comparison.
24:12 Jordan: quick note on security review — you mentioned telemetry can't leave EU, we can deploy Private control plane in eu-west and ensure logs stay in-region.
24:35 Marcus: yes please include that in the checklist.
24:48 Priya: switching back to bench results — here's an example bench row (reading): Orchid-7B q4f on A100: p50 48ms, p95 121ms, p99 187ms, tokens/sec 145; on A10G scaled we expect ~1.4x slower by architecture difference — that's a rough estimate.
25:25 Marcus: those are promising numbers if they hold on A10G.
25:35 Samir: for A10G driver issues do you have a patch list?
25:42 Priya: yes we maintain a compatibility KB and drivers list, we'll share a link; Jordan will attach to next email.
26:00 Rui: any concerns about tokenizer changes mentioned earlier?
26:10 Priya: tokenizer changes are optional — Optimize suggests small token merges to reduce token count, but we keep original tokenization for canary runs to compare. you can pin tokenizers per route.
26:40 Marcus: how do we validate semantic quality? automated checks are ok but we need a quick human review plan.
26:55 Priya: we recommend a 50-sample human eval for each quant profile initially plus metric checks (embedding similarity > 0.92 on your benchmark). Optimize will run the similarity comparisons.
27:25 Jordan: let's talk pricing briefly: for Hosted you pay per-token and there's no commit; Dedicated has commit tiers that reduce unit cost; Private is licensing plus infra. i'll send a simple model for your expected qps.
27:55 Marcus: fine. for procurement we need an estimate of TCO for 6 months.
28:05 Jordan: we'll produce hypothetical TCO with dedicated vs hosted assumptions. action: Jordan to send TCO spreadsheet.
28:20 Rui: about the bench — are you able to run a trace replay with our real traces in your secure environment or do you run bench on our infra?
28:38 Priya: we offer both: you can run on Redwood-hosted private benches (we can sign an NDA and run in eu), or we can provide the bench harness for you to run internally. typical pattern: we run initial bench with redacted traces, then hand you the harness for internal validation.
29:05 Samir: any required software we need to install to run the harness?
29:20 Priya: bench harness is a small container and a replay tool; it needs Docker and NV drivers; we'll give a runbook.
29:42 Marcus: timeline recap — if we share traces tomorrow, when can we expect bench results?
29:55 Priya: with traces Friday-ish we can return initial results in 7 business days; full trace-replay and variant tuning in 10-12 business days.
30:18 Jordan: let's capture the next steps now.
30:26 Priya: action items: Marcus to upload traces, Jordan to share SOC2 and driver KB, Priya to run bench and share results.
30:40 Marcus: i'll get the traces to you by Tuesday.
30:52 Rui: we'll obfuscate PII and truncate logs as per your spec.
31:05 Lena: one more thing — are there limits on number of custom quant profiles? our ops team likes to try 3-5 variations.
31:20 Priya: no hard limit, the runtime supports many profiles but too many increases management surface; we recommend 2-3 per model family for pilot.
31:45 Samir: what about support SLAs for Dedicated?
31:55 Jordan: Dedicated plans include a support SLA option (4-hour or 1-hour for critical incidents) depending on package. we'll include SLA options in Jordan's follow-up.
32:15 Marcus: ok, show me the CSV export one more time, specifically the compat notes column.
32:28 Priya: (scroll) compat notes include driver caveats, kernel fallback suggestions and a rough confidence score. sample note: "A10G driver 470: q4f requires custom cudnn patch; fallback to q8 recommended until patch applied". apologies if patch names look odd in the CSV.
33:05 Rui: curious about monitoring — if we enable embedding drift alerts will we get daily emails?
33:18 Priya: yes you can configure frequency and thresholds; alerts can be routed to slack, pagerduty, or email.
33:35 Marcus: ok, i'm mostly convinced. two blockers: bench on A10G to confirm p99 and legal review of open model license.
33:50 Jordan: we'll tackle both. Jordan will share license metadata and Priya will run A10G-focused bench.
34:05 Priya: for the bench i'll need a small sample trace and notes on driver versions and env.
34:18 Marcus: noted.
34:35 Rui: any final questions on rollout safety? we need auto-rollback if semantic fails.
34:50 Priya: yes the rollout includes auto-rollback criteria based on your metrics and a manual kill switch.
35:05 Jordan: before we wrap, quick product note — we just added a dev preview for kernel-wise auto-selection per request; it's labeled experimental and not on by default.
35:25 Lena: experimental is fine for pilot, but we won't enable in prod.
35:35 Jordan: understood.
35:50 Marcus: ok everyone, thanks for the walkthrough. recap and next steps?
36:00 Jordan: recap: 1) Priya will run bench for Orchid-7B q4f and 3B q8 on A10G assumptions; 2) Marcus share traces and driver list by Tue; 3) Jordan sends SOC2, driver KB, and pricing/TCO by Friday; 4) schedule latency deep-dive next week with Samir and Priya.
36:28 Marcus: sounds good.
36:34 Rui: one last nit — can you include an example of the fallback event in the export so our SREs can parse alerts?
36:46 Priya: yes i'll include sample events with schema.
36:55 Jordan: ok that's everything, we'll follow up in email. thanks all.
37:10 (meeting continues with a short Q&A and then wrap)
38:00 Rui: quick question — what's the recommended batch size for chat flows on small models to hit p99 targets?
38:20 Priya: depends heavily on request length; for your median 16-64 tokens we suggested batch 1-4, with per-route thresholds; Optimize will tune automatically during load testing.
38:50 Marcus: any gotchas with tokenization-based token count reduction?
39:05 Priya: sometimes merges can break certain domain tokens — we always run a canary to ensure semantic metrics stay within threshold.
39:30 Samir: are there any observability costs? like extra storage for token-level traces?
39:45 Jordan: yes you can opt into different retention tiers. long retention increases cost; we recommend 30-90 days for pilot.
40:10 Lena: that's fine.
40:20 Rui: ok please add the runbook for bench harness to the next email.
40:30 Priya: will do.
40:40 Jordan: any other open items?
40:50 Marcus: none from me.
41:00 Lena: no.
41:10 Samir: good.
41:20 Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll close out and send notes.
41:30 (call ends at ~15:52 UTC)
